The React Frontend internship in short

In the SkillMe React Frontend internship you build one of 3 projects, such as OmniStore: Modern Next.js E-Commerce & SaaS Marketplace, a project where you build a small online store in React where shoppers can browse products, fill a cart and go through a practice checkout. In week 1 you set up a React project with Vite and build the store's home page from small, reusable components: a header, a product card and a product grid. By week 4 you move the cart into React Context so any page can use it, save it in localStorage, and build a practice checkout form with validation. Each milestone is posted on LinkedIn and checked against that week's checklist before it counts. Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month.

Week by week

What each week of the React Frontend internship covers

Shown for OmniStore: Modern Next.js E-Commerce & SaaS Marketplace. The other projects follow the same four-week shape.

  1. Week 1 of 4

    Product Grid with Components & Props

    Beginner2-3 hours

    Set up a React project with Vite and build the store's home page from small, reusable components: a header, a product card and a product grid. You will learn how React breaks a page into pieces and passes data between them.

    What you learn

    • Creating and running a React project with Vite
    • Writing components in JSX
    • Passing data to components with props
    • Rendering lists with .map() and the key prop

    What you submit

    • A Vite + React project that runs with npm run dev
    • Header, ProductCard and ProductGrid components in separate files
    • A styled grid of at least 8 products from a local data file
    • A short demo video or screenshots of the store page
    How week 1 is reviewed
    • The app starts with npm run dev without errors
    • Each component lives in its own file under src/components
    • ProductCard gets all its data through props (no hard-coded product text)
    • The browser console shows no 'unique key' warning
    • Adding a product to the data file makes a new card appear

    Stretch goal: Add a Footer component and a small badge on cards for products marked as onSale.

  2. Week 2 of 4

    Shopping Cart & Search with State

    Beginner+2-3 hours

    Make the store interactive by adding a working cart and a search box using React state. You will learn how state makes the UI update automatically and how to share state between components.

    What you learn

    • Storing changing data with the useState hook
    • Handling click and input events in React
    • Lifting state up to a parent component and passing functions as props
    • Calculating derived values like cart totals from state

    What you submit

    • Add-to-cart buttons on every product
    • A cart panel with quantity controls, remove buttons and a live total
    • A header cart count that updates instantly
    • A working search box and a demo video of the cart in action
    How week 2 is reviewed
    • Adding the same product twice increases its quantity instead of adding a duplicate row
    • Reducing quantity to 0 removes the item from the cart
    • The total price and header count are always correct
    • Search filters products as you type and shows a 'No products found' message when nothing matches
    • State is never changed directly (no cart.push)

    Stretch goal: Add category filter buttons that work together with the search box.

  3. Week 3 of 4

    Real Products, Detail Pages & Routing

    Intermediate2-3 hours

    Replace your local data with real products from the free DummyJSON API and add a separate page for each product using React Router. You will learn how React apps load data and move between pages without reloading.

    What you learn

    • Fetching data inside useEffect and storing it in state
    • Showing loading and error states while data loads
    • Client-side routing with React Router (Routes, Route, Link)
    • Reading URL parameters with useParams

    What you submit

    • A product grid loaded from the DummyJSON API
    • A product detail page for every product at /product/:id
    • Loading and error messages on both pages
    • A demo video browsing from the grid to a product and back
    How week 3 is reviewed
    • The home page shows products from the API, not the local file
    • Clicking a card opens its detail page without a full page reload
    • Refreshing on a detail page still shows the correct product
    • A failed request shows an error message instead of a blank screen
    • Visiting an unknown URL shows a Not Found page

    Stretch goal: Fetch categories from https://dummyjson.com/products/categories and add a category filter.

  4. Week 4 of 4

    Global Cart with Context & Checkout

    Intermediate+2-3 hours

    Move the cart into React Context so any page can use it, save it in localStorage, and build a practice checkout form with validation. You will finish with a complete, deployed mini store and a clear README.

    What you learn

    • Sharing state across pages with createContext and useContext
    • Syncing state to localStorage with useEffect
    • Building and validating a controlled form
    • Deploying a Vite app to a free host

    What you submit

    • A CartContext used by every component that needs the cart
    • A cart that survives a page refresh
    • A validated checkout form and an order confirmation page
    • A live URL and a README with screenshots
    How week 4 is reviewed
    • No component receives cart data or functions through props anymore
    • Refreshing the page keeps the cart contents
    • Submitting the checkout with invalid data shows field-level errors
    • A valid order clears the cart and shows a confirmation
    • The deployed app works, including refreshing on a detail page

    Stretch goal: Add a coupon code field that applies a 10% discount for the code SKILLME10.

Is it for you?

Who the React Frontend internship is for, and what you leave with

This internship fits you if

  • You know the basics of React 18, Next.js and TypeScript and want a real project to show for it, not more tutorials.
  • You can start at beginner level. Week 1: Set up a React project with Vite and build the store's home page from small, reusable components: a header, a product card and a product grid.
  • You want to reach intermediate+ level in four weeks. Week 4: Move the cart into React Context so any page can use it, save it in localStorage, and build a practice checkout form with validation.
  • You can give it about 2-3 hours a week around college or a job, from any country.

React Frontend internship: questions and answers

What will I build in the React Frontend internship?

You are assigned one of 3 projects: OmniStore: Modern Next.js E-Commerce & SaaS Marketplace, StreamVibe: Interactive Media & Video Streaming Hub or RecipeBox: Recipe Finder & Meal Planner. Each is a single project built up over four weekly milestones, so each week adds to the last.

What skills will I learn in the React Frontend internship?

The React Frontend internship works with React 18, Next.js and TypeScript. Week 1: creating and running a React project with Vite; writing components in JSX. Week 2: storing changing data with the useState hook; handling click and input events in React. Week 3: fetching data inside useEffect and storing it in state; showing loading and error states while data loads. Week 4: sharing state across pages with createContext and useContext; syncing state to localStorage with useEffect.

Do I need experience to apply for the React Frontend internship?

You need the basics of React 18, Next.js and TypeScript, not prior internship experience. Week 1 starts at beginner level, where you set up a React project with Vite and build the store's home page from small, reusable components: a header, a product card and a product grid. Week 4 reaches intermediate+ level. A short screening quiz (8 questions, about 5 minutes) checks you are ready to start.

How is each React Frontend milestone reviewed?

Every week has a checklist, and a milestone is approved only when it meets all of it. For week 1 of OmniStore: Modern Next.js E-Commerce & SaaS Marketplace, that means: the app starts with npm run dev without errors; each component lives in its own file under src/components; ProductCard gets all its data through props (no hard-coded product text); the browser console shows no 'unique key' warning; adding a product to the data file makes a new card appear. Reviewers include engineers who work at Walmart, Google and LinkedIn, and work that misses the bar comes back with notes.

What can I put on my resume after the React Frontend internship?

Each approved milestone gives you a line you can back up with a public LinkedIn post: Set up a React project with Vite and built a product catalogue for an online store; Broke the UI into reusable components and passed data with props; Rendered a dynamic product grid from a data file using map and keys; Built a working shopping cart in React using the useState hook; Lifted state up to share cart data between the product grid, header and cart panel; Added live product search with controlled inputs; Connected my React store to the DummyJSON API using useEffect and fetch; Added product detail pages with React Router and URL parameters; Handled loading and error states for a smoother shopping experience; Built a complete React e-commerce store with a global cart using Context; Persisted the cart with localStorage and added a validated checkout flow; Deployed OmniStore live with product pages, search and cart.

What are the other projects in the React Frontend internship?

StreamVibe: Interactive Media & Video Streaming Hub: Build a Netflix-style app in React to browse TV shows, watch a trailer, filter by genre and keep your own watchlist. RecipeBox: Recipe Finder & Meal Planner: Build a React app to search recipes, save your favourites and plan your meals for the week. Every project follows the same four-week shape, with one reviewed milestone a week.

Is the React Frontend internship paid? Is there a stipend?

Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month. It is performance-based: 8–10 interns are picked each month from those who complete the internship and hold an issued certificate. It is not paid to every intern.

How much time does it take?

4 weeks, one milestone a week, each planned for about 2-3 hours. It is fully remote and open worldwide, so you work around college or a job.
